packet.headline_seed: Google Vids now lets you star in your own AI videos
packet.description_seed: Google is adding personalized AI avatars to Vids that let users create videos starring a digital version of themselves, alongside Gemini Omni-powered tools for generating and editing videos from prompts and reference images.

what: Google Vids now lets you star in your own AI videos

clean_source_blocks.text: Google is adding personalized AI avatars to Vids that let users create videos starring a digital version of themselves, alongside Gemini Omni-powered tools for generating and editing videos from prompts and reference images.

Google is bringing Gemini Omni and personal avatars to Google Vids, expanding the app’s AI-powered video creation tools for paid users. Gemini Omni can now generate and edit clips through natural language, while personal avatars let users appear in videos without recording themselves on camera. Vids already offered Veo-powered video generation, AI presenters, screen recording, and tools for turning Slides presentations into narrated videos. Omni expands that setup into a more complete editing workflow, where users can keep refining a clip through conversation instead of rebuilding it after every change. Today we’re bringing Gemini Omni and personal avatars to Google Vids 🎥Now you can generate high-quality clips with simple prompts, chat to edit them step-by-step and create a digital avatar that looks and sounds like you. pic.twitter.com/PYyhV0dbSF

OpenAI’s Sora may have shut down, but Google apparently thinks there’s still interest in a tool that lets you star in your own AI videos. On Thursday, the tech giant announced an update to Google Vids that will allow you to create a custom digital avatar that looks and sounds like you based on a selfie and a voice recording you upload. In addition, Google said it’s bringing its multi-modal AI model Gemini Omni to Vids, letting you create videos using a combination of a written prompt and reference images you upload. Omni then mixes those inputs together to create the AI video you want. It can also be used to do things like swap out the background or fix the lighting in a video recorded on your phone, or add effects. ---

Gemini Omni was announced at Google I/O 2026 as an all-purpose content model capable of working from text, images, sketches, voice recordings, and existing footage. Inside Google Vids, users can begin by describing the clip they want and add reference images for more control over the final result. Once the first version is ready, you can continue chatting with Omni to change the background, improve the lighting, add effects, or adjust individual parts of the scene. The same tools also work on videos recorded using a phone. The conversational approach gives Omni an advantage over simpler video generators. Each new instruction builds on the last, helping preserve the look, setting, and subjects across repeated edits. It also removes much of the technical friction that comes with traditional editing software like Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or Final Cut Pro.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: TechCrunch | URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/16/google-vids-now-lets-you-star-in-your-own-ai-videos/]
OpenAI’s Sora may have shut down, but Google apparently thinks there’s still interest in a tool that lets you star in your own AI videos. Omni then mixes those inputs together to create the AI video you want. It can also be used to do things like swap out the background or fix the lighting in a video recorded on your phone, or add effects.

---

[Lähde: Digital Trends | URL: https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/you-can-now-edit-videos-in-google-vids-by-simply-describing-the-changes/]
Google is bringing Gemini Omni and personal avatars to Google Vids, expanding the app’s AI-powered video creation tools for paid users. Gemini Omni can now generate and edit clips through natural language, while personal avatars let users appear in videos without recording themselves on camera.

Vids already offered Veo-powered video generation, AI presenters, screen recording, and tools for turning Slides presentations into narrated videos. Omni expands that setup into a more complete editing workflow, where users can keep refining a clip through conversation instead of rebuilding it after every change.

Today we’re bringing Gemini Omni and personal avatars to Google Vids 🎥Now you can generate high-quality clips with simple prompts, chat to edit them step-by-step and create a digital avatar that looks and sounds like you. pic.twitter.com/PYyhV0dbSF

Gemini Omni was announced at Google I/O 2026 as an all-purpose content model capable of working from text, images, sketches, voice recordings, and existing footage. Inside Google Vids, users can begin by describing the clip they want and add reference images for more control over the final result.

Once the first version is ready, you can continue chatting with Omni to change the background, improve the lighting, add effects, or adjust individual parts of the scene. The same tools also work on videos recorded using a phone.

The conversational approach gives Omni an advantage over simpler video generators. Each new instruction builds on the last, helping preserve the look, setting, and subjects across repeated edits. It also removes much of the technical friction that comes with traditional editing software like Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or Final Cut Pro.

Personal avatars bring another interesting option to Vids. Upload a selfie and a short voice recording, type the script, and Google will create a digital version of you to deliver it on screen. The feature could come in handy for training videos, product demonstrations, company updates, or presentations where you do not have the time or equipment to record yourself properly.

Gemini Omni and personal avatars are available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and eligible Workspace business customers. Personal avatars are limited to adults in select regions and tied to the account holder’s likeness. Every generated clip also carries an invisible SynthID watermark.

---

[Lähde: Android Authority | URL: https://www.androidauthority.com/google-vids-ai-avatars-free-for-everyone-us-3678613/]
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

We’ve all sat through endless dry presentations where the key takeaways simply don’t stick. Making those bullet points into a fun video used to take a quiet room, ring lights, and hours of awkward retakes. Google Vids wants to remove that barrier.

Google announced in a blog post that Google Vids is opening up its AI avatars and video generation tools to all Google account holders in the US, at no cost whatsoever.

This video editor combines traditional timeline tools with its generative AI muscle. This means you get a digital presenter to do the heavy lifting rather than rushing to get yourself recorded. You can convert any existing Google Slides deck with a click, and Vids will automatically storyboard the content, then draft a script and insert a customizable AI spokesperson to narrate it.

Under the hood, these new features are powered by Google’s latest video generation model, Veo 3.1, and Lyria 3 for custom music scoring.

Neither are you just slapping a static face on a screen. You can tell these avatars to play with uploaded props and place them against your own backdrops, making them great for tutorials, travel vlogs or client pitches. All avatar content is also embedded with a SynthID watermark to confirm it was AI-generated, to keep things transparent.

Anyone can jump in right now, but free accounts are limited to 10 Veo video generations per month. The free AI avatars are now available for US users, with other regions to get them in the coming months. If you need more headroom, you’ll need to step up to a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription to unlock up to 1,000 generations a month.

In addition to this great opportunity to try AI avatars for yourself, Google also shares that it’s expanding avatar presets and offering new language options.

Instead of the old set of 23, Google’s now giving you 53 avatar defaults to start with, available across a variety of visual styles. And when you’re trying to reach an international audience, you can now have your avatar speak in Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Arabic, Indonesian, Russian, Dutch, Polish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese, Romanian, and Ukrainian.

Vids is bringing you more control over avatars, too, expanding support for direction to custom avatars in addition to all those presets. Users can start trying out all these changes beginning today.

payload.title: Google Vids tuo käyttäjän oman tekoälyavatarin videoihin
payload.summary: Google lisää Vids-sovellukseen henkilökohtaiset tekoälyavatarit sekä Gemini Omni -työkalut, joilla videoita voi luoda ja muokata tekstiohjeiden ja viitekuvien avulla.
payload.content:
Google laajentaa Google Vids -videosovellusta henkilökohtaisilla tekoälyavatareilla ja Gemini Omni -malliin perustuvilla luonti- ja muokkaustyökaluilla. Torstaina julkistetun päivityksen myötä maksulliset käyttäjät voivat esiintyä videoissa itsensä näköisenä ja kuuloisena digitaalisena hahmona ilman omaa kameratallennusta. Samalla videoita voi tehdä tekstiohjeiden ja viitekuvien avulla sekä muokata vaiheittain luonnollisella kielellä.

## Digitaalinen avatar luodaan kuvasta ja äänestä

Henkilökohtainen avatar luodaan käyttäjän lataamasta selfiekuvasta ja äänitallenteesta. Niiden perusteella Vids muodostaa digitaalisen hahmon, joka jäljittelee käyttäjän ulkonäköä ja ääntä ja voi esiintyä videolla tämän puolesta. Käyttäjän ei siten tarvitse kuvata omaa osuuttaan kameralla. Ominaisuus täydentää sovelluksen aiempia tekoälyesiintyjiä käyttäjäkohtaisella vaihtoehdolla.

Vids tarjosi jo ennestään Veo-malliin pohjautuvaa videontuotantoa, tekoälyjuontajia, näytön tallennusta ja työkaluja, joilla Slides-esityksistä voi tehdä selostettuja videoita. Avatar lisää valikoimaan synteettisen version käyttäjästä, kun taas Gemini Omni laajentaa työnkulkua videon ensimmäisen version tuottamisesta sen jatkuvaan hienosäätöön samassa sovelluksessa.

## Videota muokataan keskustelemalla

Käyttäjä voi aloittaa kuvailemalla haluamansa videoleikkeen ja liittämällä mukaan viitekuvia, jotka antavat lisää hallintaa lopputulokseen. Gemini Omni yhdistää kirjallisen ohjeen ja kuvat videon luomiseksi. Kun ensimmäinen versio on valmis, käyttäjä voi jatkaa keskustelua mallin kanssa ja pyytää uusia muutoksia sen sijaan, että leike rakennettaisiin jokaisen korjauksen jälkeen uudelleen alusta.

Omni voi vaihtaa videon taustan, parantaa valaistusta, lisätä tehosteita tai muuttaa kohtauksen yksittäisiä osia. Työkalut toimivat myös puhelimella kuvatussa videossa. Jokainen uusi ohje rakentuu edellisen vaiheen päälle, minkä on tarkoitus auttaa säilyttämään videon ilme, ympäristö ja kohteet johdonmukaisina useiden peräkkäisten muokkausten aikana.

Google esitteli Gemini Omnin Google I/O 2026 -tapahtumassa yleiskäyttöisenä sisältömallina, joka kykenee työskentelemään tekstin, kuvien, luonnosten, äänitallenteiden ja olemassa olevan videomateriaalin pohjalta. Vidsissä malli kokoaa nämä ominaisuudet keskustelulliseksi editointityönkuluksi: käyttäjä voi luoda leikkeen, tarkentaa sitä peräkkäisillä ohjeilla ja korjata myös valmista puhelinvideota ilman perinteisen editointiohjelman monivaiheista työskentelyä.
summary_bullets: Henkilökohtainen avatar luodaan selfiekuvasta ja äänitallenteesta.
Gemini Omni tuottaa videoita tekstiohjeiden ja viitekuvien perusteella.
Videoita ja puhelimella kuvattua materiaalia voi muokata vaiheittain keskustelemalla.
payload.journalist_note: Keskeiset ominaisuudet vahvistuvat kahdesta toimituksellisesta aineistosta. Tarkkaa saatavuusaikataulua ei sisällytetty, koska sitä ei vahvistettu lähdeaineistossa.

Vidsissä malli kokoaa nämä ominaisuudet keskustelulliseksi editointityönkuluksi: käyttäjä voi luoda leikkeen, tarkentaa sitä peräkkäisillä ohjeilla ja korjata myös valmista puhelinvideota ilman perinteisen editointiohjelman monivaiheista työskentelyä.

article.source_text:
Google is adding personalized AI avatars to Vids that let users create videos starring a digital version of themselves, alongside Gemini Omni-powered tools for generating and editing videos from prompts and reference images.

Google is bringing Gemini Omni and personal avatars to Google Vids, expanding the app’s AI-powered video creation tools for paid users. Gemini Omni can now generate and edit clips through natural language, while personal avatars let users appear in videos without recording themselves on camera. Vids already offered Veo-powered video generation, AI presenters, screen recording, and tools for turning Slides presentations into narrated videos. Omni expands that setup into a more complete editing workflow, where users can keep refining a clip through conversation instead of rebuilding it after every change. Today we’re bringing Gemini Omni and personal avatars to Google Vids 🎥Now you can generate high-quality clips with simple prompts, chat to edit them step-by-step and create a digital avatar that looks and sounds like you. pic.twitter.com/PYyhV0dbSF

OpenAI’s Sora may have shut down, but Google apparently thinks there’s still interest in a tool that lets you star in your own AI videos. On Thursday, the tech giant announced an update to Google Vids that will allow you to create a custom digital avatar that looks and sounds like you based on a selfie and a voice recording you upload. In addition, Google said it’s bringing its multi-modal AI model Gemini Omni to Vids, letting you create videos using a combination of a written prompt and reference images you upload. Omni then mixes those inputs together to create the AI video you want. It can also be used to do things like swap out the background or fix the lighting in a video recorded on your phone, or add effects. ---

Gemini Omni was announced at Google I/O 2026 as an all-purpose content model capable of working from text, images, sketches, voice recordings, and existing footage. Inside Google Vids, users can begin by describing the clip they want and add reference images for more control over the final result. Once the first version is ready, you can continue chatting with Omni to change the background, improve the lighting, add effects, or adjust individual parts of the scene. The same tools also work on videos recorded using a phone. The conversational approach gives Omni an advantage over simpler video generators. Each new instruction builds on the last, helping preserve the look, setting, and subjects across repeated edits. It also removes much of the technical friction that comes with traditional editing software like Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or Final Cut Pro.
